angularResponse.lensDescriptionInterpretation: not needed for the operator audit because the paper itself explicitly states the resulting 1.5-degree field of view

pointing.reportedQuantity: brightness B of a place in the sky
pointing.acquisition: automatic meridian sweep from horizon through zenith to horizon

spectralResponse.sourceLimitation: source states that later-twilight color correction was needed but was not applied because the sky spectral distributions were not known exactly

calibration.absoluteMethod: clear daylight sky compared with calibrated blue-filtered Macbeth illuminometer
calibration.rangeTransfer: standard tungsten lamp attenuated in a known nonselective manner for voltage, amplifier-gain, and lens-aperture changes
calibration.runCheck: small luminous radium phosphor button source

temporalResponse.tableReduction: more than 1000 record values per station were plotted versus solar altitude; smooth curves were drawn and the published Tables I/II were read from those curves

geometryConvention.definitionInSource: altitude of the Sun, positive above and negative below the horizon

provenance.observableClass: Koomen et al. 1952 JOSA 42:353-356, p.353 instrument description and p.354 definition of B; DOI 10.1364/JOSA.42.000353
provenance.angularResponse: Koomen et al. 1952 p.353 gives a circular 0.6-cm aperture and explicitly states a nominal 1.5-degree diameter field; no within-field acceptance/vignetting function recovered
provenance.pointing: Koomen et al. 1952 pp.353-354: meridian sweep through zenith; Tables I/II use sky altitude P and bearing Z
provenance.spectralResponse: Koomen et al. 1952 p.353; footnote 6 cites W. S. Plymale, Rev. Sci. Instr. 18, 535-539 (1947)
provenance.calibration: Koomen et al. 1952 p.353 calibration paragraph; no numerical calibration uncertainty recovered
provenance.temporalResponse: Koomen et al. 1952 pp.353-355; 12-second full sweep and smooth-curve table reduction are stated, exact integration/time constant is not
provenance.units: Koomen et al. 1952 p.354: B in candles per square foot
provenance.geometryConvention: Koomen et al. 1952 p.354 defines H only as solar altitude relative to the horizon; no geometric/apparent/refraction convention recovered
